title: FP16 multiplier
description: An IEEE binary16 multiplier (1 sign, 5 exponent, 10 fraction bits) with subnormal inputs and outputs, round to nearest even, canonical quiet NaN for invalid operations. The starting point is a plain readable Verilog implementation: unpack, 11x11-bit significand multiply, leading-zero count, normalise, round, pack.
flow: Yosys synthesis and OpenROAD static timing analysis on ASAP7. Correctness: the gate-level netlist is re-simulated on about 18.9 million enumerated operand pairs (every subnormal or zero operand against structured partners, plus LFSR-driven broad pairs); all checks must pass.

notes.glm-5.2: Default effort, pinned to Z.AI. The high-effort runs are recorded but held back from the table.

notes.glm-5.3-flash: Default effort, which Z.AI documents as max for this model; 13k to 18k output tokens per step, reasoning included. Pinned to Z.AI.
notes.glm-5.3-flash-high: RTLSCOUT_REASONING_EFFORT=high, one level below Z.AI's default max for this model: 2k to 6k output tokens per step against 13k to 18k for the default row. Pinned to Z.AI.
notes.deepseek-v4.1-flash: Default effort, which DeepSeek documents as high. Pinned to the CoreWeave endpoint (fp8).
notes.mimo-v2.6-flash: Default: thinking on (a toggle at Xiaomi). Pinned to Xiaomi's endpoint (fp8).

footnotes: Rows labelled as measured before the current suite are earlier data (pre-v1 seed runs from July 2026 with an unpackaged rtlscout, or suite-v1 runs from October 2026 without the provider pin and completion cap). Each is replaced when reruns of that entry under the current suite are published.
All entries were called through OpenRouter without prompt caching, so every step pays for its full input.

Until 2026-10-13 every evaluation of this task also ran rtlscout's combinational equivalence check (yosys-abc cec, 120 s), which rejected designs that restructure the significand multiplier although they passed all 18.9 million vectors. The runs made under that gate were discarded; the task runs with --skip-cec like the other three since then.
